findings.claim: lab.json claims a-dev-profile-that-keeps-endpoints-open-during-front-end-work#o1, whose catalog text is 'Define a dev-profile SecurityFilterChain that permits all requests AND allows the local front-end origin with CORS'. The lab's Task 5 (README lines 66-71) builds only permitAll with csrf disabled; no CORS configuration appears anywhere in the lab, and DevProfileSecurityTest checks only that /admin/stats and /workshops answer 200. The CORS half of the claimed objective is never practiced, so the objective binding overclaims.
findings.recommendation: Either add a minimal CORS configuration to the dev chain (e.g. an allowed origin for http://localhost:5173 asserted by the dev test with an Origin header), or narrow the claim: drop #o1 and keep #o2, recording the CORS half as covered by the topic page only.

findings.claim: lab.json claims role-protected-endpoints#o3 ('Test protected endpoints with MockMvc and Spring Security's test support for an anonymous user and users with different roles'), but the learner writes no test in this lab: SecurityLabTest.task2ProtectsEndpointsByPathAndRole ships complete and the learner only runs it. Unlike the validation and integration labs, which turn their test-writing objectives into learner-finished test files, this test-writing objective is only demonstrated to the learner, not practiced by them.
findings.recommendation: Drop role-protected-endpoints#o3 from the lab's objectives, or convert the role-matrix test into a learner-finished test (TODO-annotated like WebLayerTest/OpsIntegrationTest) so the learner writes the user()/roles() request post-processors themselves.
